factProposals.value: REQ-001 (connect to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace) is not met: no real connector exists. Building one needs a Microsoft Entra app registration, a Google Cloud OAuth client and a test account for each, which the project does not have yet.
Agents are meant to read email and documents only through a read-only connector interface (listMessages, listDocuments), never through a vendor SDK directly.

Network failures and rate limits are retried on the same agent (at most 3 attempts, backoff up to 2 s, a service's requested wait honoured up to 10 s); an unavailable, timed-out or crashing agent is taken out of rotation and its task moved to another agent with the same capability; if none is left the task fails and the operation is marked failed.
Every orchestration step is written to an append-only, hash-chained audit log; credential-like fields are redacted before they are written.
Agents declare one or more capabilities from process, risk and finance; operations are requested by a person (operations_manager in the demo) and run by the orchestrator as a system actor.

decisions.statement: Build the orchestration core behind a connector interface, with stand-in agents, instead of calling Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace directly.
decisions.rationale: No credentials or test tenants are available; the acceptance criteria can be met and tested without them. Confirmed with the student before building.

decisions.statement: Retry NetworkError and RateLimitedError on the same agent; reassign on AgentUnavailableError, TimeoutError and any unexpected error.
decisions.rationale: Network blips and rate limits are about the call, not the agent; an agent that is down, hung or crashing will not get better by being retried.

decisions.statement: Fail closed: if an audit entry cannot be written, cancel all in-flight tasks and reject the operation.
decisions.rationale: REQ-008 requires every action to be logged; carrying on unrecorded would break the guardrail.

decisions.statement: Save task results by operation id so a completed operation is replayed and a part-finished one resumes without redoing finished tasks; pass agents an idempotencyKey of operationId:taskId.
decisions.rationale: Every side effect must be idempotent; re-running must not redo work.

decisions.statement: Refuse an operation id reused with a different set of tasks (compared by a fingerprint of task ids, capabilities and inputs), and let a call for a still-running operation join that run.
decisions.rationale: Found in code review: returning or resuming old work for a changed request gives a wrong answer, and a caller retry during a run would otherwise duplicate every unfinished task.

decisions.statement: A failed agent is out of rotation for a cooldown (30 s by default), then gets one trial task at a time; success puts it back in rotation, failure restarts the cooldown, and a failed trial's task moves to another agent.
decisions.rationale: Without it, one task that crashes every agent of a capability took that capability offline until a restart (raised in code review).

limitations.statement: The only agents are demo stand-ins with scripted, made-up results; no real AI agent exists yet.
Agent health (who is out of rotation, cooldowns, trial slots) lives in memory: a restart puts every agent back in rotation.
One process may write a given audit log file at a time; concurrent writers are not supported.
The hash chain detects edits and removals anywhere except the end: deleting the last entries leaves a valid chain. Detecting that needs the latest hash anchored outside the file (STORY-006).

A second call for an operation that is still running joins the first run, but only within one process; two processes sharing a result store could both run it, as nothing provides a cross-process lock yet.
The file result store rewrites one JSON file per update, which suits a single process and modest volumes, not a shared service.
